newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia's new money expected by end 1997.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia's new money expected by end 1997.

text.p: Bosnia's new currency is expected to go into circulation by the end of 1997, the Sarajevo daily Dnevni Avaz said on Tuesday.
Kasim Omicevic, a Moslem member of the governing board of the new Bosnian Central Bank told the paper the board would finish drafting a law founding the bank by the end of January.
"Once the law is passed, the technical preparations for money printing will take six or seven months so I expect this to be implemented by the end of next year," he added.
Under the terms of the Dayton peace accord, Bosnia will have a single central bank and one currency, which will most likely have a foreign reserve backing in German Marks to make it convertible.
The bank will have an IMF-appointed foreign governor, Serge Robert of France, and one board member from each of the Serb, Moslem and Croat ethnic groups.
Officials from the Moslem-Croat federation and Serb republic are engaged in a battle over several bank related issues including the design of the new currency.
The foundation law has to be endorsed by the three-member Presidency and country's parliament, Omicevic said.
